statement: Conservation of perceived harm: as the actual prevalence of harmful items falls, the harm-classification threshold shifts downward so that total perceived harm is substantially conserved (conservation coefficient kappa >= 0.5).
scope: NEW claim, 2026-08-25. Not present in Geometric Ethics v1.24. Adjacent to, and explicitly NOT a revival of, the withdrawn GE-HARM-CONSERVATION.

evidence.note: Seal is BLOCKED on the required pilot: this programme has no verified effect size for the ethical variant under its own stimulus set. Power before bars.

Rewritten around Social-Chem-101 (/archive/ethics-corpora on Atlas, 260,627 distinct actions). Synthetic generation abandoned; generator retired to fallback. Sampling frame verified empirically: 82,757 actions survive filters, 27,323 available for the 440-item ambiguous band (62x headroom), both anchors available (1,967 benign / 5,299 severe).

history.event: OPENED as forward exposure (PE-BRW-1.0 s5.5), and only the SECOND non-retrospective row in the ledger. Prompted by recording GE-HARM-CONSERVATION: the metaphysical conservation claim is blocked on the moral metric, but the psychological claim in its neighbourhood is testable now without committing to any moral geometry.

SCOPING PREMISE ADOPTED AND RECORDED (author): 'morality hinges on what is perceived anyway, so the distinction isn't that important.' Adopted rather than argued, and recorded so it can be revisited. The perceived/actual distinction is nonetheless RETAINED IN THE DESIGN, because experimenter-set prevalence is the only non-perceptual anchor and without it kappa is not estimable -- the claim would be unfalsifiable.

REGISTERED IN ADVANCE, the tension with the RETAINED claim: under the adopted premise a positive result says the same act carries a different harm value depending on what it was judged alongside, which is prima facie a failure of invariance of harm accounting. Whether prevalence framing counts as a 'representation change' in the book's sense is undecided and MUST be decided before results are seen. This experiment may bite the claim the corpus holds, not the one it withdrew.
CLASS exploratory and it stays there. Registration is not evidence.

STAGE 0 PROTOCOL DRAFTED. Estimator VERIFIED NUMERICALLY BEFORE USE (experiments/ge007_kappa_recovery.py, seed 20260825): kappa recovered across 0.00-1.00 with a disclosed additive bias of -0.011, downward and therefore conservative against the 0.5 bar. Degenerate-case gate exercised under a weak manipulation and fires as intended. Two design failure modes identified and gated: (1) an item pool dense at the extremes rather than the ambiguous middle has NO resolution for threshold shift regardless of true effect size; (2) mid-scale CONTESTED items (bimodal, raters disagree) are not continuum positions and can mimic threshold shift with no concept change -- excluded by SD and dip test, and reported separately rather than discarded, since disagreement about what is harmful is independently interesting to this corpus.

STAGE 0 REWRITTEN AROUND A REAL CORPUS; SYNTHETIC GENERATION ABANDONED. The generator composed items from a frame, a population and an ethical feature, which are NOT semantically independent -- a records-only study cannot enrol at a bedside, a zebrafish study has no rabbits. Three keyword screens were added, each AFTER READING SAMPLES rather than by prior design, and each caught a class the previous missed; a fresh sample after the third still contained obvious contradictions. Every structural check passed throughout. THE FINDING: semantic incoherence is invisible to structural verification, and the failure is silent -- incoherent items produce rater disagreement that mimics genuine contestedness, which the dip test would then exclude, deleting real continuum coverage while appearing to work. Real situations are coherent by construction, which removes the failure class rather than screening it.

CORPUS SUBSTITUTES FOR AUTHORING, NOT FOR NORMING. kappa compares each participant's threshold against per-item harm values, which must be on this study's scale, from this study's population, under this study's instructions. Imported labels satisfy none. Design accordingly over-samples 1,200 items for 800 slots, norms all 1,200 on a 0-100 scale, and selects after norming but BEFORE the main run -- fixed in advance, since the same selection after main-run data would not be legitimate.

CORRECTION FOUND IN THE SOURCE ANNOTATIONS. `action-agree` is ANTICIPATED agreement -- one worker's prediction of consensus -- not observed agreement. Where agreement IS observable (24,013 actions with >=2 independent annotations), 46.5% disagree outright on the judgment label. The field is therefore demoted to a sampling prior and is NOT the contestedness screen; the screen remains this study's own norming SD and dip test. The multi-annotated subset becomes a calibration set, checkable before any main-run data, reported whichever way it falls. Also: 89.5% of actions carry a single annotation, so within-item annotator variance is unavailable for most of the pool -- which is why norming cannot be skipped.

LIMITATION REGISTERED IN ADVANCE: RANGE COMPRESSION COSTS POWER. Social-Chem-101's severe end tops out at ordinary interpersonal wrongs, not atrocities, so the harm continuum is truncated relative to the synthetic pool it replaces. A compressed range gives the threshold less room to travel and SHRINKS the effect the pilot must detect. Registered so that a small kappa is not later attributed to absence of the phenomenon when it may reflect the instrument's range. Also registered: US/English/self-selected population, and care-harm dominance in the source's moral-foundation distribution.
